title: MERN Stack
body:
[[MongoDB]]
[[Express]]
[[React]]
[[Node.js|Node]]

---

Four technologies that between them cover a whole web application in one language. That is the
selling point: [[JavaScript]] on the client, on the server, and in the database's query
language, so nobody has to context-switch at the boundary.

| Letter | Piece | Job |
|---|---|---|
| M | [[MongoDB]] | the database. Documents rather than tables, essentially [[JSON]] |
| E | [[Express]] | routing and middleware on top of Node |
| R | [[React]] | the [[Client]]-side interface |
| N | [[Node.js]] | the server runtime everything after M runs on |

It was "all the rage" in about 2015, per [[Express]]. What made it a movement rather than four
libraries is that it was the first mainstream stack where the frontend developer and the
backend developer could be the same person without either learning a second language.

The data path is worth tracing once, because it is the whole course in one line: [[React]]
calls [[Fetch]], which sends [[HTTP]] to an [[Express]] route, which queries [[MongoDB]], which
returns documents, which Express sends back as [[JSON]], which React renders. Every arrow in
that sentence has a note.

Variants swap one letter: MEAN puts Angular in R's place, and PERN puts PostgreSQL in M's.
See [[MERN]] and [[Web Application]].
